title: Shared VPC and VPC peering: one network across several projects

videos.script: One company, several projects, one network. That is Shared VPC. {{shared}} A host project owns the network, its subnets and its firewall. Service projects put their machines in it, and pay for them. {{host}} The role that matters every day is Network User, granted on one subnet. A team can put machines there, and nowhere else. {{user}} Peering is the other answer. Two networks, two owners, maybe two companies, joined so their machines talk on internal addresses. {{peering}} Both sides have to agree. No range may overlap. And peering is not transitive. {{rules}} If the planner peers with a partner and with analytics, those two still cannot reach each other through the planner. {{transitive}} You check all three rules with a short program before anyone creates anything. {{program}} And the company the planner just bought numbered its network the planner's way. That one waits for a renumbering. {{end}}
